issue_context.title: Windows Authentication -  ((ClaimsPrincipal)User).IsInRole
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
User.IsInRole works with ActiveDirectory Group Names on local development machine, but does not work with ActiveDirectory Group Names after deploying to onpremise windows IIS server.  However, ActiveDirectory Group Sid does work on onpremise windows IIS server.  

### To Reproduce
Asp.Net Core 3.1 Blazor Server 
WindowsAuthentication: true
AnonymousAuthentication: false
var authenticationState = await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync()
var b = authenticationState.User.IsInRole("MyAdGroupName")
b is true on local development machine, but false on windows IIS server

### Further technical details

3.1

Windows Authentication is rather "special". It, as you have discovered, caches roles as SIDs and only does the lookup against role names when IsInRole is called. If it's a claims principal it can't do that, claims principal doesn't know how to call out to AD, so it needs to be cast back. 

Make sure it's not null though when you cast it, if something has fiddled with it (Claims transformation, or something else) then it will stay as a claims identity and you'd need to figure out what did that and stop it.

> looks like this is back in your court. How is Blazor capturing the user?

We receive `IHubContext.User` from SignalR when the circuit is being started up, and make that object available to user code. We pass through the same actual object - we don't clone it or anything like that.

Here's the flow:

1. When starting the circuit, `StartCircuit` passes `Context.User` to `CreateCircuitHost`: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/116799fa709ff003781368b578e4efe2fa32e937/src/Components/Server/src/ComponentHub.cs#L117
2. `CreateCircuitHost` passes that object to `SetCircuitUser`: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4a7bf75e89e3dfe7264a641ed041f50788d28d20/src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/CircuitFactory.cs#L87
3. `SetCircuitUser` uses that object to initialize an `AuthenticationState` instance and passes it to `SetAuthenticationState`: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/271ebe019823e8e6a751429cd350c2db76ebab05/src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/CircuitHost.cs#L485-L486
4. `SetAuthenticationState` holds this info and supplies it to any user code that accesses the authentication state via `AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync`: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/057ec9cfae1831f91f1a0e01397059b20431db7b/src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/ServerAuthenticationStateProvider.cs#L25

Since Blazor doesn't transform the `ClaimsPrincipal` object in any way, but rather just passes through what it gets from `IHubContext.User` into user code, I'm not sure what we could be doing to prevent this from working. @Tratcher do you have any thoughts on anything we might be doing wrong? Are we right to expect the `IHubContext.User` instance to remain valid for the duration of a SignalR connection? (Note that we do renew the instance to whatever `IHubContext.User` has become each time the user reconnects - this flow starts [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/116799fa709ff003781368b578e4efe2fa32e937/src/Components/Server/src/ComponentHub.cs#L171)).

> User = (await AuthenticationStateTask.ConfigureAwait(false)).User;

@roysurles I don't know this has anything to do with the problem you're reporting, but you definitely shouldn't use `ConfigureAwait(false)` with Blazor or any other UI stack. If you want lots more info about why, read [this FAQ](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/configureawait-faq/). Using `ConfigureAwait(false)` with a UI stack exposes you to synchronization context errors.
@BrennanConroy? I know SignalR does lots of special things to handle WindowsPrincipals. Not sure how many of them Blazor benefits from for free?

@bmoteria Check what the server is actually responding with when you make your request to the API endpoint. The error message `'<' is an invalid start of a value` suggests it's returning HTML when you're expecting JSON, so it may well be misconfigured routes.

@SteveSandersonMS the api endpoint returns json when navigate directly to uri. When httpclient was trying to request data it wasn't in json format therefore error occurred. After specifying default request header, it's working.

> Note that in my case it always executes if.. code.

Right, if you're using WindowsAuth + LongPolling then it always will hit that (until we fix it).

On a related note, Blazor generally works better with WebSockets (less latency) and it also wont hit the WindowsAuth issue. You should consider enabling WebSockets in IIS.

> Are you tracking this issue elsewhere (so I can close this issue), or would you prefer to leave this one open to track that underlying issue?
